best_for: Ruby and Rails developers who want one IDE for Ruby, the front end and the database, and who either code for fun or can expense a JetBrains subscription.
description:
RubyMine is the IDE for Ruby and Rails from JetBrains, the company behind IntelliJ IDEA and PyCharm. Students and teachers can get it free as part of JetBrains' All Products Pack. If you pay for a subscription for a full year without a break, you keep a perpetual license to the version you had when it ends.

A built-in Git screen lets you commit, branch and settle merge conflicts, and it also works with Mercurial, Perforce and Subversion. You can run and debug your code inside a dev container, in WSL, or on a remote machine over SSH. Search finds any class, method or usage in your project. You can also hand tasks to AI agents such as Claude, Codex, Gemini or Junie, and send notes on a diff back to them.

points.title: Free for hobby work, with strings
points.text: Personal, non-commercial use is free: learning, unpaid open source, hobby projects and content creation. You must sign in with a JetBrains Account, the license runs a year and renews only if used in the last 6 months, and the IDE sends anonymous usage statistics you cannot turn off.

points.title: Paid work needs a subscription
points.text: Individuals pay USD 109 for the first year, then 87 and 65 in later years, or USD 10.90 a month. Organizations pay USD 269 per user per year or USD 26.90 a month. A 30-day trial is offered. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Rails in depth
points.text: It understands Rails, Hotwire, RBS, Rake and RuboCop, with type-aware completion and inspections. A graphical test runner handles RSpec, Minitest, Cucumber and Test::Unit, and the debugger covers Ruby and JavaScript.

points.title: Front end and database included
points.text: WebStorm's JavaScript and TypeScript support comes built in, along with React, Vue and Angular. You can browse and query PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB and SQLite without a separate tool.

points.title: Plan for 8 GB of RAM
points.text: JetBrains asks for 8 GB of memory with 3 GB free for the IDE, 10 GB of disk and a 4-core CPU. Supported systems are Windows 10 and 11 and macOS 26 and 27. Java is bundled, so nothing else is needed.

points.title: Builds on this page
points.text: Windows installers come for x64 and Arm64, per user or machine-wide; the Mac builds are separate Intel and Apple silicon disk images. JetBrains also ships Linux tarballs and a Snap, which this site does not list.

points.title: Downgrades on Windows and Mac
points.text: The Windows listing goes back to 2020.3 and macOS lists about 100 recent releases, with the ones winget and Homebrew lack taken from JetBrains' own release feed. JetBrains' Toolbox App can also install a specific older version.
